newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Phnom Penh airport may open by Wednesday - official.
newsitem.headline: Phnom Penh airport may open by Wednesday - official.

text.p: Cambodia's international airport, closed by fighting since Saturday, should reopen within two days, a civil aviation official said on Monday.

Keo Sophal, the director general of the Civil Aviation Authority, said the Phnom Penh airport would be repaired after being looted and damaged over the weekend and should be open for flights by Tuesday or Wednesday.

"Last night illegal forces controlled the airport and broke equipment and looted because they were drunk," Keo Sophal said, referring to forces loyal to First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh. "Now government troops control it again and we will start repairs. We hope to open tomorrow or the day after."

Forces loyal to Ranariddh withdrew from a key military base just a few km (miles) from the airport on Sunday night, leaving the area under the control of forces loyal to Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.
Fighting between the two sides broke out on Saturday, prompting airlines to cancel all flights to and from Phnom Penh.

One aviation source in Cambodia said the runway was damaged by shelling and said he doubted commercial airplanes could land. Keo Sophal said all equipment in the terminal building had been looted or broken.
